description: Fascon 1.0 (Rust-like syntax, memory-safe without lifetime annotations → readable C): arenas and bump arenas with generation-tagged Ids, own trees and own_alloc, MMIO regions and x86 I/O ports (port_io), bare metal on x86_64 and AArch64 through the Fascon virtual BIOS (QEMU), type inference without annotations, names without @, free declaration order, automatic reframing of plain Rust syntax, the strict Fascon form for functional-safety review, diagnostics with root-cause timelines, verified quick fixes and a reference dictionary. Includes the 0.1.0 engine for 0.1 files.
command.showDictionary: Open the Dictionary as a Table
command.searchDictionary: Search the Dictionary (keywords, error codes, second-class references)
command.lookupWord: Look Up the Word at the Cursor
command.explainAtCursor: Explain Error (timeline, fixed code, mathematical explanation)
command.associateRs: Treat .rs Files in This Workspace as Fascon
config.language.auto: Follow the VS Code display language
config.language: Display language of Fascon (diagnostics, explanations, dictionary, menus)
config.serverPath: Path to the fascon executable (empty = use the Windows / Linux / macOS binary bundled with the extension)
config.cacheLine: Cache-line alignment (alignas) of Process / Kernel allocations. 128 for Apple M-series or Intel adjacent-line prefetching, 32 for Cortex-M7/R5
config.barrierPolicy: Memory-barrier policy of the generated C code
config.barrierPolicy.strict: Compiler barriers at region boundaries + acquire/release for hand-offs between CPUs (recommended)
config.barrierPolicy.paranoid: Also a full hardware fence at every region boundary (for debugging, slow)
config.isrCapacity: Isr region capacity (bytes). Exceeding it is F0900
config.outDir: Output directory for C code (relative to the workspace). The source file is never overwritten
command.hostRun: Run on This PC (screen saved as PNG)
command.qemuRun: Boot in QEMU (target from settings; portable = BIOS-less AArch64)
command.qemuScreenshot: Boot in QEMU and Save Screenshots (headless, target from settings)
command.newExample2: Open a 1.0 Example (kernel / GUI / dual-architecture / BIOS / Rust style / app / callbacks)
config.extraPath: Folders added to PATH when Fascon runs QEMU and C compilers (e.g. C:\Program Files\qemu, C:\Program Files\LLVM\bin)
config.screenshotFrames: Number of screens to save with "Boot in QEMU and Save Screenshots" (one per FASCON-GUI-READY line)
config.qemuTimeout: Time limit in seconds for headless QEMU runs
config.columns: Give each `for id in a` reduction a column holding just the values it reads (scans then read only that column; the slots stay authoritative). Off = the 1.0.0 tables and scans (--columns off)
config.cpu: CPU for "Run on This PC": compile the generated C for this PC's CPU (-march=native / -mcpu=native: AVX2 / AVX-512 / NEON widths for column scans) or for the baseline of the architecture
config.cpu.native: This PC's CPU (fastest; the program may not run on older CPUs)
config.cpu.baseline: The architecture's baseline (runs on any x86-64 / AArch64)
command.qemuRunX86: Boot in QEMU (x86_64, Fascon virtual BIOS)
command.qemuRunArmBios: Boot in QEMU (AArch64, Fascon virtual BIOS)
command.buildBios: Build BIOS Images for x86_64 and AArch64 (one source)
command.emitStrict: Show the Strict Fascon Form (functional-safety review)
command.toggleReframing: Toggle Automatic Reframing (plain Rust syntax) for This Workspace
config.target: Target of the generated C for I/O ports (port_io) and of "Boot in QEMU": portable = both forms selected by #if (QEMU: BIOS-less AArch64), x86_64 = in / out instructions (QEMU pc + Fascon virtual BIOS), aarch64 = ports remapped to MMIO (QEMU virt + Fascon virtual BIOS)
config.target.portable: Both architectures (#if); QEMU boots BIOS-less AArch64
config.target.x86_64: x86_64: com1 = c; becomes out dx, al; QEMU pc with the Fascon virtual BIOS
config.target.aarch64: AArch64: ports remapped to MMIO (COM1 → PL011); QEMU virt with the Fascon virtual BIOS
config.reframing: Automatic reframing: rewrite ordinary Rust syntax (static mut + link_section, macros, println! formatting, unsafe, pub, char literals, lifetimes) into Fascon before compiling. auto = follow #![reframing(rust)] at the top of each file
config.emitStrictOnBuild: Also write <name>.strict.fsc (the strict Fascon form) when generating C
command.buildBoard: Build a real-hardware image for a board (--board: ELF + raw .img)
command.qemuBoard: Boot on a board's QEMU machine (--board)
command.pkgLabel: Label the package safety (Pure Safe / Low-Level / Hardware)
command.stackReport: Prove the maximum stack depth (call graph, --target rtos)
command.qemuGenericOs: Boot in QEMU with the generic-os BSP (PAN, PAC, BTI, guard pages, W^X)
config.profile: OS profile: classic keeps the generated C of existing programs unchanged; rtos (32-bit Ids, recursion ban, stack proof) or generic-os (64-bit Ids, per-CPU magazines, RCU, PAC/BTI). A `// fascon-target:` line in the file takes precedence.
config.gc: fascon-gc: off = --gc=off (gc_arena is rejected with F2623; no GC runtime is linked)
config.board: Default board package for the board commands (name under boards/ or a path to board.toml); empty = ask
